common_name: Tallulah Sunrise Azalea (Peachy-Orange Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in dappled shade to morning sun, giving the open, upright habit room to fill in over several seasons.

directions: An Aromi-breeding-line native hybrid azalea, Tallulah Sunrise opens large peachy-pink trusses that unfurl to reveal a brighter orange throat with peachy-pink stamens, creating a distinctive two-tone bloom in mid-spring before or as the leaves emerge. The deciduous shrub builds an open, airy framework over time rather than a dense mound, so it reads best planted among other woodland-edge natives rather than as a tight hedge. Give it humus-rich, acidic soil and morning sun with afternoon shade, and avoid disturbing the shallow root zone once established.

common_name: Clear Creek Azalea (Fragrant Yellow Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; this is one of the larger-growing Aromi hybrids, so allow generous space from structures and paths.

directions: Clear Creek is a soft-yellow-flowered selection from the Aromi native azalea breeding line, producing rounded clusters of fragrant, trumpet-shaped blooms with a deeper yellow blotch and white throat in mid-spring. It grows considerably larger than many of its siblings in the group, eventually forming a small multi-stemmed tree-like shrub rather than a compact border plant. As with other deciduous native hybrids in this line, it performs best in humus-rich, acidic soil with filtered light and should not be crowded given its eventual size.

common_name: Radiant Red Azalea (Fiery Red Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in dappled shade to morning sun.

directions: Radiant Red is one of the more saturated-color selections from the Aromi native azalea breeding line, setting deep red buds in late winter that open in early-to-mid spring into brilliant, fiery-red, single trumpet-shaped flowers with a spicy fragrance. Like its relatives, it blooms on bare wood ahead of or alongside new foliage, giving a strong burst of color against the still-dormant garden. It tolerates more heat, humidity, and part shade than many evergreen azaleas, making it a good choice for Gulf Coast and Southeastern gardens with acidic, humus-rich soil.

common_name: Four Kings Azalea (Yellow-and-Red Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; this vigorous, larger-growing Aromi selection needs ample room to mature.

directions: Four Kings is a vigorous, large-growing selection from the Aromi native azalea breeding line, opening bright yellow, trumpet-shaped flowers touched with a faint red flush and a deep golden-yellow blotch on bare branches in early-to-mid spring. The large, spicy-sweet scented blooms appear in dense rounded clusters, and the shrub can eventually reach small-tree proportions, so it suits a woodland garden or background planting better than a tight foundation bed. Give it acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil and part shade for the best bloom and heat tolerance.

common_name: Linda Guy Azalea (Fragrant True-Pink Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in dappled shade to morning sun.

directions: Named for Linda Guy, a horticulturist who helped propagate and distribute Dr. Eugene Aromi's native azalea seedlings from Mobile, Alabama, this cultivar is known for having some of the largest flowers and trusses in the whole Aromi breeding line. Red buds open in early-to-mid spring into large, spicy-sweet scented, true-pink flowers marked with a golden-yellow blotch. It shares the group's tolerance for heat and humidity, performing best in acidic, humus-rich soil with filtered morning sun and afternoon shade.

common_name: Tangerine Delight Azalea (Orange Native Flame Azalea Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil with even moisture; this large-growing native hybrid needs room to reach its full size.

directions: A hybrid selection of the native flame azalea (Rhododendron calendulaceum), Tangerine Delight produces brilliant orange-to-peach, sweetly spicy-fragrant flowers in mid-spring on a dense, upright, eventually large shrub. It is noted among deciduous native azaleas for good heat tolerance combined with cold hardiness well into the mountain South, and it attracts bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds. Grow it in acidic, humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in bright shade to part sun for the strongest bloom.
